pipelines.summary: Updated existing single-ship result components to display absolute metrics from backend. PhysicsOverview now shows top speed and acceleration using AbsoluteMetricCard components with context phrases (e.g., 'corvette range', 'nimble') when an engine is selected. EnginePerformanceDisplay displays top speeds for all flight modes (normal, reverse, boost, travel) alongside existing TWR display. All absolute metrics are additive - existing percentage-based displays remain intact. Conditional rendering ensures no 'null' or 'N/A' clutter when engine not selected.

comments.note: PhysicsOverview.tsx - Absolute metrics section is separated from base metrics with pt-4 border-t. Clear visual hierarchy. Context phrases use getSpeedContext() and getAccelerationContext() from WP-005 utility.

EnginePerformanceDisplay.tsx - Top speeds section clearly labeled 'Top Speeds by Flight Mode'. Normal flight uses ValueComparison to show original→adjusted delta. Reverse/boost/travel modes display single values (no comparison since backend doesn't calculate adjusted values for these modes).

EnginePerformanceDisplay.tsx - Null checks on all top speed fields prevent rendering empty/undefined values. hasTopSpeedData flag controls entire section visibility. Follows existing pattern from TWR display section.

ResultsPanel.tsx - shipSize prop defaults to 'M' if not provided. Prevents crashes when shipDetails is null during initial load. shipSize passed through to PhysicsOverview for accurate context phrase generation.

All components use TypeScript strict mode with proper interface definitions. No any types introduced. Conditional rendering (?? operator, optional chaining) ensures type safety when fields are null/undefined.

comments.description: TypeScript compilation error TS18048: 'enginePerformance.topSpeed' and 'enginePerformance.topSpeedAdjusted' are possibly 'undefined'. The interface defines these as 'topSpeed?: number | null' which means they can be undefined OR null. The code checks 'topSpeed !== null' which narrows away null but NOT undefined, leaving unsafe access.
comments.fix: Change condition from 'topSpeed !== null && topSpeedAdjusted !== null' to 'topSpeed != null && topSpeedAdjusted != null' (loose equality) OR 'topSpeed !== null && topSpeed !== undefined && topSpeedAdjusted !== null && topSpeedAdjusted !== undefined'.

comments.description: TypeScript compilation error TS18048: 'enginePerformance.topSpeedReverse', 'topSpeedBoost', and 'topSpeedTravel' are possibly 'undefined'. Same root cause as above — checking != null doesn't narrow away undefined in strict mode.
comments.fix: Change all null checks from strict '!== null' to loose '!= null' which narrows away both null and undefined: 'topSpeedReverse != null', 'topSpeedBoost != null', 'topSpeedTravel != null'.

pipelines.summary: WP-007 FAILED QA validation. TypeScript compilation fails with 6 errors in EnginePerformanceDisplay.tsx due to unsafe optional property access. Root cause: Interface defines properties as 'field?: number | null' but code only checks strict '!== null', which doesn't narrow away 'undefined'. TypeScript strict mode correctly flags this as unsafe. Fix required: use loose equality '!= null' instead of strict '!== null', which narrows away both null and undefined in one check.

artifacts.purpose: Fixed TypeScript strict mode errors by replacing strict null checks with loose null checks that properly narrow both null and undefined

pipelines.summary: Fixed TypeScript compilation errors in EnginePerformanceDisplay.tsx. Changed all strict null checks (!== null) to loose null checks (!= null) on lines 87, 96, 104, and 112. This correctly narrows away both null and undefined values for optional properties typed as 'field?: number | null'. TypeScript strict mode's type narrowing requires this approach when dealing with properties that can be both null and undefined. Verified: npx tsc --noEmit passes cleanly.

comments.note: EnginePerformanceDisplay.tsx - Using loose equality (!= null) is the idiomatic TypeScript approach for checking optional properties that can be null or undefined. Single check narrows away both, cleaner than 'field !== null && field !== undefined'.

This is a common TypeScript pattern when interfacing with backend APIs that may omit fields (undefined) or explicitly return null. Loose equality handles both cases elegantly while satisfying strict mode type narrowing.

comments.description: Verified fix: All null checks changed from strict (!== null) to loose (!= null) equality. Properly narrows away both null and undefined. TypeScript strict mode type narrowing satisfied.
